Let's do the math. You have 3.5 years so around 42 months. In these 42 months, you will be putting in 21 lakhs as per your monthly SIP. At 20% xirr, this can become \~34-35 lakhs Your 25 lakhs will have 3.5 years to compound. Using the rule of 72, you will need 20% XIRR for your 25 lakhs to double in 3.5 years. I would say 20% xirr is a good number to target; it won't be easy and you will need to stay disciplined and concentrated, which you have already started doing. All this amounts to \~85 lakhs. You can get very close to 1 cr if you can get 20% XIRR and be consistent with 50K monthly SIP. Free advice: Focus on consistency and target stable returns. Don't chase risky assets and don't churn too much; give your investments time to compound meaningfully. You already have a great head start in terms of your age. You have at least 25 years of compounding journey left. At 20% xirr, in 25 years, your money can multiply by a factor of \~140x. Even if you stop doing SIPs from now on, your corpus will become 35-40 crore.

FD isn’t as safe as you think — inflation eats it all | Pehle mujhe bhi lagta tha FD is the safest option. 6.5% fixed return sunke lagta tha — tension-free hai. Lekin jab maine inflation aur tax ka impact samjha, tab pata chala FD safe nahi, deceptively risky hai. Long-term average inflation = ~7% Most FDs return = ~6.5% (pre-tax) Post-tax return aur kam ho jaata hai Matlab real return negative hai. 25 saal baad ₹1 lakh ki FD ka real value ₹88,000 ke aas-paas ho jaata hai — aur woh bhi best case scenario me. FD paisa save karta hai, grow nahi. Agar tera goal sirf paisa bachana hai short term ke liye — emergency fund, 6-12 months ke liye — tab theek hai. Lekin long-term ke liye? Better options available hain — jaise SIP in index funds, equity mutual funds, etc. FD se paisa secure nahi hota — sirf ruk jaata hai. Aur rukhe hue paisa ka value har din kam hota jaata hai.
